about: Short plain-English labels for the States table and state overview pages. Every label summarizes a rule already recorded in docs/data/audit-fields.json, docs/data.js or the v3 coverage research; nothing here is new research. Fields: labor = how the warranty hourly rate is set; requests = how often a dealer may ask for a new rate; parts = parts markup rule; response = manufacturer response (only when the structured fields need a plain-English override); hours = paid-hours note (only when it adds something); multiplier = labor-time multiplier (omitted = none in statute). Update the state's entry whenever enacted law changes one of these rules.

AK.labor: At least retail rate for similar work, unless agreed
AK.hours: Independent guide is the floor unless agreed

CA.hours: Blanket percentage cuts to repair time prohibited

CT.labor: Retail rate from prior month's ROs

DE.response: Takes effect within 30 days; information requests restart the clock

FL.labor: Agreed rate; otherwise the greater of two statutory methods
FL.parts: Agreed markup; otherwise the greatest of three statutory methods
FL.response: 30 days to negotiate; otherwise the statutory rate controls

GA.requests: 1 per calendar year (parts, labor or both)

HI.labor: Equal to retail rate (no more, no less)
HI.requests: No labor-rate request process (parts markup: 1 per 12 months)
HI.parts: At least retail markup, if reasonable

ID.response: May request more information within 30 days; rate takes effect within 90 days (no rejection process)

IL.labor: Same effective rate as customer-pay repairs
IL.hours: 1.5 × OEM time only if no guide is agreed or it omits the repair
IL.multiplier: Yes: 1.5 × OEM time, only when no time guide is agreed or the agreed guide does not cover the repair

IA.response: May audit within 30 days; no decision deadline

KS.response: May audit within 30 days; no decision deadline

KY.labor: Reasonable; retail rate and filed schedule are benchmarks
KY.requests: No request frequency or sample in statute
KY.parts: Retail benchmark; statute cites cost plus 30% gross profit

ME.requests: No labor-rate request process (parts markup: 2 per calendar year)

MI.response: 45 days to approve or contest; deemed approval for labor is an inference

MN.labor: Effective retail rate, at dealer's election (otherwise reasonable)
MN.parts: Cost plus reasonable markup, or retail method at dealer's election

MS.labor: Retail rate, on dealer's written request
MS.hours: Benchmarked to a qualified technician, not the dealer's clock

MO.labor: Reasonable; retail rate is a primary factor
MO.parts: Reasonable; retail parts charges are a primary factor

MT.hours: Dealer picks the OEM guide or its customer-pay guide

NE.labor: Reasonable; prevailing community rates are the principal factor; floor is dealer's own retail or fleet rate
NE.requests: No labor-rate request limit or procedure (parts markup: 2 per calendar year)
NE.parts: At least retail or fleet charges
NE.response: May request up to 100 more ROs (once per 12 months), then 30 days to rebut

NV.requests: No request frequency or sample in statute

NJ.labor: Average retail rate (labor sales ÷ billed hours)
NJ.requests: 2 per calendar year (rate, parts and time combined)
NJ.response: Audit of dealer's sample only; effective 30 days after declaration
NJ.hours: Dealer may elect a retail ÷ OEM hours ratio
NJ.multiplier: Yes: the dealer may apply for a time multiplier equal to customer-billed hours ÷ OEM hours for the same sampled repairs, applied to OEM warranty times (effective April 1, 2026)

NY.response: No rebuttal deadline; effective 30 days after declaration
NY.hours: The guide the dealer uses for customer-pay repairs

NC.hours: Documented requests for more time may not be unreasonably denied

ND.requests: Not within 12 months of the last declaration

OR.requests: 1 per year (franchises entered or renewed from Jan 1, 2026)

PA.hours: Factory time; statute sets no reasonableness standard

RI.labor: Retail rate from prior month's ROs

SC.parts: Cost plus retail markup, on request
SC.response: May request documents within 30 days; no decision deadline

SD.requests: No request frequency or sample in statute

TN.labor: At least retail rate; capped at posted rate
TN.requests: No labor-rate request process (sworn rate filed with Commission)
TN.response: Must show the Commission the rate is improper; no deadline

TX.labor: Comparable retail rate; floor is the greater of two averages
TX.parts: Retail floor; no fixed markup stated

VT.requests: No labor-rate request process (parts markup: 2 per calendar year)

VA.parts: Retail markup, by agreement or statutory average

WA.requests: 1 increase per calendar year (labor and parts each)

WV.requests: Not within 12 months of the last declaration

WI.labor: Retail labor sales ÷ OEM hours (normalized rate)
WI.response: 30 days; must start paying the substantiated rate
WI.hours: OEM time; retail difference is built into the rate
WI.multiplier: No separate multiplier: the retail-to-OEM time difference is built into the hourly rate. Do not apply it twice.

WY.labor: Dealer submission or agreement; may not exceed retail
